docs.title: OmniVault
docs.text: OmniVault is a unified Go library for secret management across multiple providers. It provides a single interface for accessing secrets from password managers, cloud secret managers, enterprise vaults, and local storage.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Unified Interface - Single API for all secret storage backends
  • Extensible Architecture - Add custom providers as separate Go modules without modifying the core library
  • URI-Based Resolution - Reference secrets using URIs like op://vault/item/field or aws-sm://secret-name
  • Built-in Providers - Environment variables, file-based, and in-memory storage included
  • Zero External Dependencies - Core library has no external dependencies beyond the standard library
  • CLI Tool - Command-line interface with encrypted local storage and daemon architecture
  • Secure Local Storage - AES-256-GCM encryption with Argon2id key derivation

docs.title: As a Go Library
docs.text:
Import OmniVault into your Go application to access secrets from multiple providers:

import "github.com/plexusone/omnivault"

client, _ := omnivault.NewClient(omnivault.Config{
    Provider: omnivault.ProviderEnv,
})

secret, _ := client.Get(ctx, "API_KEY")
fmt.Println(secret.Value)

docs.text:

docs.title: init
docs.text:
Initialize a new vault with a master password.

omnivault init
  • Prompts for master password (minimum 8 characters)
  • Prompts to confirm password
  • Creates encrypted vault at ~/.omnivault/
  • Vault is unlocked after initialization

Requires Daemon

The daemon must be running before initialization.

docs.title: unlock
docs.text:
Unlock the vault with the master password.

omnivault unlock
  • Prompts for master password
  • Vault stays unlocked until locked or auto-lock timeout

docs.title: lock
docs.text:
Lock the vault immediately.

omnivault lock
  • Clears encryption key from memory
  • Secrets are inaccessible until unlocked

docs.title: status
docs.text:
Show vault and daemon status.

omnivault status [--format <format>]

Flags:

Flag Description --format Output format: text (default), json, yaml

Examples:

# Default text output
omnivault status

# JSON output for scripting
omnivault status --format json

Example text output:

Daemon: running
Uptime: 1h23m45s
Vault: unlocked
Secrets: 12
Unlocked at: 2024-01-15 09:00:00

Status fields:

Field Description Daemon running or not running Uptime Time since daemon started Vault locked, unlocked, or not initialized Secrets Number of stored secrets (when unlocked) Unlocked at Timestamp of last unlock

docs.title: passwd
docs.text:
Change the vault master password.

omnivault passwd
  • Prompts for current password
  • Prompts for new password (minimum 8 characters)
  • Prompts to confirm new password
  • Re-encrypts all secrets with the new password

Vault Must Be Unlocked

The vault must be unlocked to change the password.

Example:

omnivault passwd
# Enter current password: ********
# Enter new password (min 8 chars): ********
# Confirm new password: ********
# Password changed successfully!

docs.title: get
docs.text:
Retrieve a secret value.

omnivault get <path> [--format <format>] [--field <name>]

Arguments:

Argument Description path Secret path (e.g., database/password)

Flags:

Flag Description --format Output format: text (default), json, yaml, shell --field Extract a specific field from the secret

Examples:

# Get secret value
omnivault get api/key

# JSON output
omnivault get database/credentials --format json

# YAML output
omnivault get database/credentials --format yaml

# Shell-sourceable output
omnivault get aws/keys --format shell
# Output:
# export AWS_KEYS='...'
# export AWS_KEYS_ACCESS_KEY='AKIA...'
# export AWS_KEYS_SECRET_KEY='...'

# Extract specific field
omnivault get database/credentials --field password

# Use in scripts
DB_PASS=$(omnivault get database/credentials --field password)

Shell Format:

The shell format outputs export statements that can be sourced directly:

# Source secrets into environment
eval $(omnivault get aws/keys --format shell)

# Or save to file and source
omnivault get aws/keys --format shell > /tmp/aws-env
source /tmp/aws-env

Expiry Warnings:

If a secret has an expiration date and is expired or expiring soon, a warning is printed to stderr:

WARNING: Secret 'api/token' expires in 5 days (on 2024-01-20)

docs.title: set
docs.text:
Store a secret.

omnivault set <path> [value]

Arguments:

Argument Description path Secret path (e.g., database/password) value Optional secret value

If value is not provided, you'll be prompted to enter it (input is hidden).

Examples:

# Prompted input (recommended for sensitive values)
omnivault set database/password

# Direct value
omnivault set config/timeout 30

# Piped input
echo "my-secret" | omnivault set api/key

docs.title: list
docs.text:
List all secrets or filter by prefix.

omnivault list [prefix] [--format <format>] [--metadata]

Arguments:

Argument Description prefix Optional path prefix filter

Flags:

Flag Description --format Output format: text (default), json, yaml --metadata Show detailed metadata (timestamps, full tags)

Examples:

# List all secrets
omnivault list

# List secrets under database/
omnivault list database/

# JSON output for scripting
omnivault list --format json

# Show detailed metadata
omnivault list --metadata

Default Output:

database/password (value+fields)
database/username
api/key [production, v2]
config/timeout

4 secret(s)

With --metadata:

database/password (value+fields) [env=production, service=api]
  Created: 2024-01-01T10:30:00Z
  Updated: 2024-01-15T15:45:00Z
  Expires: 2024-06-01T00:00:00Z
database/username
  Created: 2024-01-01T10:30:00Z
  Updated: 2024-01-01T10:30:00Z

2 secret(s)

Indicators:

  • (value+fields) - Secret has both value and fields
  • (fields) - Secret has only fields
  • [tag1, tag2] - Secret tags (keys only)
  • [key=value] - Full tag pairs (with --metadata)

docs.title: delete
docs.text:
Delete a secret.

omnivault delete <path>

Aliases: rm

Arguments:

Argument Description path Secret path to delete

Prompts for confirmation before deletion.

Examples:

omnivault delete api/old-key
omnivault rm database/test

docs.title: search
docs.text:
Search for secrets by path pattern.

omnivault search <pattern> [--regex] [--format <format>]

Arguments:

Argument Description pattern Search pattern (glob or regex)

Flags:

Flag Description --regex Use regex pattern instead of glob --format Output format: text (default), json, yaml

Examples:

# Glob pattern (default)
omnivault search "database/*"
omnivault search "*password*"
omnivault search "api/v*"

# Regex pattern
omnivault search ".*prod.*" --regex
omnivault search "^api/v[0-9]+/" --regex
omnivault search "(database|cache)/.*password" --regex

# JSON output for scripting
omnivault search "database/*" --format json

Output:

database/prod/password
database/prod/username
database/dev/password

3 secret(s) found

docs.title: export
docs.text:
Export secrets as JSON.

omnivault export [prefix] [--output <file>]

Arguments:

Argument Description prefix Optional path prefix filter

Flags:

Flag Description --output Output file (default: stdout)

Examples:

# Export all secrets to stdout
omnivault export

# Export to file
omnivault export --output backup.json

# Export subset with prefix
omnivault export database/ --output database-backup.json

# Pipe to another command
omnivault export | jq '.secrets | length'

Output Format:

{
  "secrets": [
    {
      "path": "database/password",
      "value": "secret123",
      "fields": {
        "username": "admin"
      },
      "tags": {
        "env": "production"
      }
    }
  ],
  "count": 1
}

Sensitive Data

The export contains plaintext secrets. Handle with care and delete backup files securely.

docs.title: import
docs.text:
Import secrets from JSON.

omnivault import [file] [--merge]

Arguments:

Argument Description file Input file (default: stdin)

Flags:

Flag Description --merge Skip existing secrets instead of overwriting

Examples:

# Import from file (overwrites existing)
omnivault import backup.json

# Import with merge (skip existing)
omnivault import backup.json --merge

# Import from stdin
cat secrets.json | omnivault import

# Pipe from export
omnivault export | omnivault import --merge

Confirmation:

Import always prompts for confirmation:

Import 5 secret(s)? (existing secrets will be overwritten) [y/N]: y
Imported: 5, Skipped: 0, Errors: 0

With --merge:

Import 5 secret(s)? (merge mode - existing secrets will be skipped) [y/N]: y
Imported: 2, Skipped: 3, Errors: 0

docs.text:
Start the daemon in background.

  • Writes PID to ~/.omnivault/omnivaultd.pid

docs.text:
Stop the daemon.

omnivault daemon stop
  • Locks the vault before stopping
  • Removes socket and PID files

docs.title: daemon status
docs.text:
Show daemon status.

omnivault daemon status

docs.title: daemon run
docs.text:
Run the daemon in foreground.

omnivault daemon run

Useful for debugging. Press Ctrl+C to stop.

docs.title: version
docs.text:
Show version information.

omnivault version

docs.title: help
docs.text:
Show help information.

omnivault help
omnivault -h
omnivault --help

docs.title: Output Formats
docs.text:
Commands that support --format accept the following values:

Format Description text Human-readable format (default) json JSON output yaml YAML output shell Shell-sourceable export statements (get only)

The default format can be set in the configuration file.

docs.title: Exit Codes
docs.text: Code Description 0 Success 1 Error (message printed to stderr)

docs.title: Environment Variables
docs.text: Currently, the CLI does not use environment variables for configuration. Use the configuration file instead.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: OmniVault supports user configuration via a JSON configuration file.

docs.title: Configuration File
docs.text:
The configuration file is located at:

Platform Path macOS/Linux ~/.omnivault/config.json Windows %LOCALAPPDATA%\OmniVault\config.json

docs.title: Creating the Configuration
docs.text:
Create the configuration file manually:

mkdir -p ~/.omnivault
cat > ~/.omnivault/config.json << 'EOF'
{
  "auto_lock_timeout": "15m",
  "default_format": "text",
  "expiry_warning_days": 30
}
EOF

docs.title: auto_lock_timeout
docs.text:
Duration before the vault auto-locks due to inactivity.

Type Default string (duration) "15m"

Format: Go duration string (e.g., "5m", "1h", "30m", "2h30m")

Examples:

{
  "auto_lock_timeout": "30m"
}

{
  "auto_lock_timeout": "1h"
}

Activity Reset

Each secret operation (get, set, list, delete, search) resets the auto-lock timer.

docs.title: default_format
docs.text:
Default output format for commands that support --format.

Type Default string "text"

Valid Values: "text", "json", "yaml"

Example:

{
  "default_format": "json"
}

This affects:

  • omnivault get (also supports "shell")
  • omnivault list
  • omnivault status
  • omnivault search

Override with Flag

The --format flag always overrides the default.

docs.title: expiry_warning_days
docs.text:
Number of days before expiration to show warnings when retrieving secrets.

Type Default integer 30

Example:

{
  "expiry_warning_days": 14
}

When you get a secret that expires within this many days, a warning is printed to stderr:

WARNING: Secret 'api/token' expires in 5 days (on 2024-01-20)

Set to 0 to only warn about already-expired secrets.

docs.title: default_tags
docs.text:
Tags automatically applied to all new secrets.

Type Default object null

Example:

{
  "default_tags": {
    "managed_by": "omnivault",
    "environment": "development"
  }
}

These tags are merged with any tags specified when creating a secret.

docs.title: Complete Example
docs.text:
{
  "auto_lock_timeout": "30m",
  "default_format": "json",
  "expiry_warning_days": 14,
  "default_tags": {
    "managed_by": "omnivault"
  }
}

docs.title: Configuration Precedence
docs.text:
1. Command-line flags (highest priority)
  2. Configuration file
  3. Built-in defaults (lowest priority)

docs.title: Validating Configuration
docs.text:
The configuration file is read on each command. Invalid JSON will cause an error:

omnivault status
# Error: failed to load config: invalid character...

Validate your configuration:

cat ~/.omnivault/config.json | python3 -m json.tool

docs.title: File Permissions
docs.text:
The configuration file should have restricted permissions:

chmod 600 ~/.omnivault/config.json

While the configuration itself doesn't contain secrets, restricting access follows the principle of least privilege.

docs.title: Reloading Configuration
docs.text: Configuration is loaded fresh on each command invocation. No restart is required after changes.

docs.title: Configuration vs. Vault Settings
docs.text:
Setting Stored In Scope Auto-lock timeout Config file User preference Default format Config file User preference Expiry warnings Config file User preference Master password Vault (encrypted) Security Secrets Vault (encrypted) Data

The configuration file controls CLI behavior. The vault stores encrypted secrets and security parameters.

docs.title: Daemon Architecture
docs.text: The OmniVault CLI uses a daemon (background service) architecture for secure secret management.

docs.title: Why a Daemon?
docs.text:
The daemon architecture provides several security benefits:

  1. Session-Based Unlock - Unlock once, access secrets multiple times without re-entering password
  2. Memory Protection - Encryption keys stay in daemon memory, not in CLI process
  3. Auto-Lock - Automatic locking after inactivity
  4. Single Point of Control - One process manages all vault access

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
┌─────────────┐     Unix Socket      ┌──────────────┐
│  omnivault  │ ◄──────────────────► │  omnivaultd  │
│    (CLI)    │      HTTP/JSON       │   (Daemon)   │
└─────────────┘                      └──────┬───────┘
                                            │
                                            ▼
                                     ┌──────────────┐
                                     │ ~/.omnivault │
                                     │  vault.enc   │
                                     │  vault.meta  │
                                     └──────────────┘
  1. CLI sends commands to daemon via Unix socket (macOS/Linux) or TCP (Windows)
  2. Daemon holds encryption key in memory
  3. Daemon performs all cryptographic operations
  4. Files on disk are always encrypted

docs.title: Unix Socket
docs.text:
On macOS and Linux, the daemon listens on a Unix socket:

~/.omnivault/omnivaultd.sock

Unix sockets provide:

  • Local-only access (no network exposure)
  • File permission-based security
  • Fast IPC performance

docs.title: HTTP API
docs.text:
The daemon exposes an HTTP API over the socket:

Endpoint Method Description /status GET Daemon and vault status /init POST Initialize new vault /unlock POST Unlock vault /lock POST Lock vault /secrets GET List secrets /secret/:path GET Get secret /secret/:path PUT Set secret /secret/:path DELETE Delete secret /stop POST Stop daemon

docs.title: Starting
docs.text:
omnivault daemon start
  1. Checks if daemon is already running
  2. Starts new process in background
  3. Creates Unix socket
  4. Writes PID file

docs.title: Running
docs.text:
While running, the daemon:

  • Listens for CLI commands
  • Manages vault lock state
  • Resets auto-lock timer on activity
  • Holds encryption key in memory (when unlocked)

docs.title: Stopping
docs.text:
omnivault daemon stop
  1. Sends stop command via socket
  2. Daemon locks vault (clears key from memory)
  3. Daemon shuts down HTTP server
  4. Removes socket and PID files

docs.title: Graceful Shutdown
docs.text:
On SIGINT or SIGTERM:

  1. Vault is locked
  2. Active requests complete
  3. Socket is removed
  4. Process exits

docs.title: Auto-Lock
docs.text: The daemon automatically locks the vault after a period of inactivity.

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
• Timer starts when vault is unlocked
  • Each vault operation resets the timer
  • When timer expires, vault is locked
  • Default timeout: 15 minutes

docs.title: Activity Reset
docs.text:
These operations reset the auto-lock timer:

  • get - Reading a secret
  • set - Writing a secret
  • delete - Deleting a secret
  • list - Listing secrets

These operations do NOT reset the timer:

  • status - Checking status
  • lock - Manual lock
  • unlock - Already unlocked

docs.title: Files
docs.text:
The daemon creates and manages these files:

File Purpose Permissions ~/.omnivault/ Config directory 700 vault.enc Encrypted secrets 600 vault.meta Salt and parameters 600 omnivaultd.sock Unix socket 600 omnivaultd.pid Daemon PID 644

docs.title: macOS / Linux
docs.text:
• Uses Unix socket at ~/.omnivault/omnivaultd.sock
  • Standard Unix permissions apply
  • Process daemonization via Setpgid
  • Graceful shutdown via SIGTERM

docs.title: Windows
docs.text:
• Uses TCP on 127.0.0.1:19839
  • Vault files stored in %LOCALAPPDATA%\OmniVault\
  • Process termination via Process.Kill()
  • No socket file (TCP-based IPC)
Feature macOS/Linux Windows IPC Unix Socket TCP localhost Address ~/.omnivault/omnivaultd.sock 127.0.0.1:19839 Config Dir ~/.omnivault/ %LOCALAPPDATA%\OmniVault\ Shutdown SIGTERM Process.Kill()

docs.title: Debugging
docs.text:
Run the daemon in foreground to see logs:

omnivault daemon run

Example output:

Starting OmniVault daemon...
INFO daemon started socket=/Users/you/.omnivault/omnivaultd.sock
INFO vault unlocked
INFO secret accessed path=database/password
INFO vault auto-locked due to inactivity

docs.title: Socket Permissions
docs.text:
The Unix socket is created with permissions 600:

  • Only the owner can connect
  • Other users cannot access the daemon

docs.title: Memory Security
docs.text:
When locked:

  • Encryption key is zeroed from memory
  • No secrets can be decrypted
  • Vault file remains encrypted

docs.title: No Network Access
docs.text:
The daemon:

  • Never listens on network interfaces
  • Only accepts local Unix socket connections
  • Cannot be accessed remotely

docs.title: CLI Quick Start
docs.text: This guide shows you how to use the omnivault command-line tool for secure local secret management.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
go install github.com/plexusone/omnivault/cmd/omnivault@latest

Verify the installation:

omnivault version

docs.title: 1. Start the Daemon
docs.text:
The CLI requires a background daemon for secure operations:

omnivault daemon start

docs.title: 2. Initialize Your Vault
docs.text:
Create a new vault with a master password:

omnivault init

You'll be prompted to enter and confirm a master password (minimum 8 characters).

Remember Your Password

The master password is never stored. If you forget it, you cannot recover your secrets.

docs.title: 3. Store a Secret
docs.text:
# Prompted for value (hidden input)
omnivault set database/password

# Or provide value directly
omnivault set api/key sk-12345

docs.title: 4. Retrieve a Secret
docs.text: omnivault get database/password

docs.title: 5. List Secrets
docs.text:
# List all secrets
omnivault list

# List secrets with a prefix
omnivault list database/

docs.title: 6. Delete a Secret
docs.text:
omnivault delete database/password

You'll be asked to confirm before deletion.

docs.title: Lock the Vault
docs.text:
Lock the vault to protect your secrets:

omnivault lock

docs.title: Unlock the Vault
docs.text:
Unlock to access secrets again:

omnivault unlock

docs.title: Check Status
docs.text:
View vault and daemon status:

omnivault status

Example output:

Daemon: running
Uptime: 2h30m15s
Vault: unlocked
Secrets: 5
Unlocked at: 2024-01-15 10:30:00

docs.title: Output Formats
docs.text:
Get secrets in different formats:

# Default text output
omnivault get database/credentials

# JSON output
omnivault get database/credentials --format json

# YAML output

docs.title: Security Model
docs.text: OmniVault uses industry-standard cryptographic practices to protect your secrets.

docs.title: Algorithm
docs.text:
AES-256-GCM (Galois/Counter Mode)

  • 256-bit key size
  • Authenticated encryption (integrity + confidentiality)
  • Random 12-byte nonce per secret
  • NIST-approved algorithm

docs.title: Key Derivation
docs.text:
Argon2id - Winner of the Password Hashing Competition

Parameter Value Purpose Time 3 iterations CPU cost Memory 64 MB Memory cost (GPU resistance) Threads 4 Parallelism Key Length 32 bytes 256-bit key Salt 32 bytes Random per vault

These parameters follow OWASP recommendations for password hashing.

docs.title: Why Argon2id?
docs.text:
Argon2id is resistant to:

  • GPU attacks - High memory requirement makes parallel attacks expensive
  • ASIC attacks - Memory-hard function is difficult to optimize in hardware
  • Side-channel attacks - Data-independent memory access pattern
  • Time-memory tradeoff - Hybrid approach resists both

docs.title: Never Stored
docs.text:
The master password is:

  • Used only to derive the encryption key
  • Never written to disk
  • Never logged or displayed
  • Cleared from memory after key derivation

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
Password correctness is verified by:

  1. Deriving key from entered password
  2. Attempting to decrypt a known "magic" value
  3. Using constant-time comparison to prevent timing attacks
// Constant-time comparison prevents timing attacks
subtle.ConstantTimeCompare(decrypted, expectedMagic)

docs.title: Minimum Requirements
docs.text:
• Minimum 8 characters
  • No maximum length
  • Any characters allowed

Strong Passwords

Use a passphrase of 4+ random words for better security and memorability.

docs.title: File Structure
docs.text:
macOS / Linux:

~/.omnivault/
├── vault.enc           # Encrypted secrets
├── vault.meta          # Unencrypted metadata
├── omnivaultd.sock     # Unix socket (runtime)
└── omnivaultd.pid      # PID file (runtime)

Windows:

%LOCALAPPDATA%\OmniVault\
├── vault.enc           # Encrypted secrets
├── vault.meta          # Unencrypted metadata
└── omnivaultd.pid      # PID file (runtime)

docs.title: vault.meta (Unencrypted)
docs.text:
Contains non-sensitive metadata:

{
  "version": 1,
  "created_at": "2024-01-15T10:00:00Z",
  "salt": "base64-encoded-32-bytes",
  "argon2_params": {
    "time": 3,
    "memory": 65536,
    "threads": 4,
    "key_len": 32
  },
  "verification": "base64-encrypted-magic"
}

The verification field is an encrypted known value used to verify passwords.

docs.title: vault.enc (Encrypted)
docs.text:
Contains encrypted secrets:

{
  "secrets": {
    "path/to/secret": "base64-nonce+ciphertext+tag"
  }
}

Each secret value is:

  1. Serialized to JSON
  2. Encrypted with AES-256-GCM
  3. Base64 encoded

docs.title: File Permissions
docs.text: File Mode Description ~/.omnivault/ 700 Owner only vault.enc 600 Owner read/write vault.meta 600 Owner read/write omnivaultd.sock 600 Owner only

docs.title: Key Handling
docs.text:
When locked:

// Zero out key before releasing
for i := range key {
    key[i] = 0
}
key = nil

docs.title: Daemon Isolation
docs.text:
• Encryption key exists only in daemon memory
  • CLI never sees the raw key
  • Key is zeroed on lock or shutdown

docs.title: Brute Force
docs.text:
Argon2id parameters make brute force expensive:

  • Each attempt requires 64 MB RAM
  • Each attempt takes ~1 second on modern hardware
  • Cannot be parallelized efficiently

docs.title: Offline Attacks
docs.text:
If an attacker obtains vault.enc and vault.meta:

  • Must still brute force the password
  • Argon2id parameters are public but still protective
  • Strong password makes attack infeasible

docs.title: Replay Attacks
docs.text:
Each encryption uses a random nonce:

  • Same plaintext produces different ciphertext
  • Replaying old ciphertext is detectable (wrong nonce)

docs.title: Tampering
docs.text:
AES-GCM provides authentication:

  • Any modification to ciphertext fails decryption
  • Cannot alter secrets without the key

docs.title: Password Selection
docs.text:
• Use a strong, unique password
  • Consider a passphrase (4+ random words)
  • Use a password manager for the master password

docs.title: Physical Security
docs.text:
• Lock your workstation when away
  • Use full disk encryption
  • Don't leave vault unlocked unnecessarily

docs.title: Backup
docs.text:
• Back up ~/.omnivault/ directory
  • Store backups securely (encrypted)
  • Remember: backup is useless without password

docs.title: Regular Rotation
docs.text:
Consider changing your master password periodically:

# Future feature
omnivault change-password

docs.title: Protected Against
docs.text:
• Unauthorized file access (secrets encrypted)
  • Memory dumps of CLI process (key in daemon)
  • Network attacks (Unix socket only)
  • Tampering (authenticated encryption)
  • Brute force (Argon2id)

docs.title: Not Protected Against
docs.text:
• Keyloggers capturing password
  • Compromised daemon process
  • Physical access to unlocked machine
  • Forgotten password (no recovery)
  • Sophisticated malware with root access

docs.title: Comparison
docs.text: Feature OmniVault macOS Keychain 1Password Encryption AES-256-GCM AES-256-GCM AES-256-GCM KDF Argon2id PBKDF2 Argon2id Open Source Yes No No Local Only Yes Yes No Cross-Platform Yes macOS only Yes

docs.title: Client API
docs.text: The OmniVault client provides a high-level API for secret management.

docs.title: Creating a Client
docs.text:
// With a built-in provider
client, err := omnivault.NewClient(omnivault.Config{
    Provider: omnivault.ProviderEnv,  // or ProviderFile, ProviderMemory
})

// With a custom provider
client, err := omnivault.NewClient(omnivault.Config{
    CustomVault: myCustomProvider,
})

Always Close

Always call client.Close() when done to release resources.

docs.title: Get
docs.text:
Retrieve a secret by path:

secret, err := client.Get(ctx, "path/to/secret")
if err != nil {
    if err == vault.ErrSecretNotFound {
        // Secret doesn't exist
    }
    // Handle other errors
}

docs.text:

secret := &omnivault.Secret{
    Value: "my-secret-value",
}

docs.text:
Remove a secret:

err := client.Delete(ctx, "path/to/secret")

docs.text:
Check if a secret exists:

exists, err := client.Exists(ctx, "path/to/secret")

docs.title: List
docs.text:
List secrets by prefix:

paths, err := client.List(ctx, "database/")
// Returns: ["database/password", "database/username", ...]

docs.text:
Get just the string value:

value, err := client.GetValue(ctx, "API_KEY")

docs.text:
Get a specific field from a multi-field secret:

docs.text:

docs.text:
Variants that panic on error (useful for initialization):

// Panics if secret not found or error occurs
secret := client.MustGet(ctx, "REQUIRED_SECRET")
value := client.MustGetValue(ctx, "REQUIRED_VALUE")

Must variants should only be used during application startup or in contexts where a missing secret is truly fatal.

docs.title: Secret Structure
docs.text:
type Secret struct {
    // Primary value
    Value string

    // Binary value (alternative to Value)
    ValueBytes []byte

    // Additional fields (for multi-field secrets)
    Fields map[string]string

    // Metadata
    Metadata Metadata
}

type Metadata struct {
    // Custom tags
    Tags map[string]string

    // Timestamps (set automatically)
    CreatedAt  *time.Time

}

docs.title: Accessing Values
docs.text:
secret, _ := client.Get(ctx, "path")

// Primary value as string. fmt and log/slog print "[REDACTED]" for a
// secret, so it cannot leak into logs by accident.
value := secret.Reveal()

// Primary value as bytes
bytes := secret.Bytes()

// Specific field
field := secret.GetField("username")

// Check if field exists
if val, ok := secret.Fields["password"]; ok {
    // Use val
}

docs.text:
secret, err := client.Get(ctx, "path")
if err != nil {
    switch err {
    case vault.ErrSecretNotFound:
        // Secret doesn't exist
    case vault.ErrAccessDenied:
        // Permission denied
    default:
        // Other error
    }
}

docs.title: Provider Capabilities
docs.text:
Check what operations a provider supports:

caps := client.Capabilities()

if caps.Write {
    // Provider supports writing secrets
}

if caps.List {
    // Provider supports listing secrets
}

type Capabilities struct {
    Read       bool  // Can read secrets
    Write      bool  // Can write secrets
    Delete     bool  // Can delete secrets
    List       bool  // Can list secrets
    Binary     bool  // Supports binary values
    MultiField bool  // Supports multiple fields per secret
}

docs.title: Custom Providers
docs.text: Create your own secret provider by implementing the vault.Vault interface.

docs.title: Interface
docs.text:
package vault

type Vault interface {
    // Get retrieves a secret by path
    Get(ctx context.Context, path string) (*Secret, error)

    // Set stores a secret at the given path
    Set(ctx context.Context, path string, secret *Secret) error

    // Delete removes a secret
    Delete(ctx context.Context, path string) error

    // Exists checks if a secret exists
    Exists(ctx context.Context, path string) (bool, error)

    // List returns paths matching the prefix
    List(ctx context.Context, prefix string) ([]string, error)

    // Name returns the provider name
    Name() string

    // Capabilities returns supported operations
    Capabilities() Capabilities

    // Close releases resources
    Close() error
}

docs.title: 1. Create a new Go module
docs.text:
mkdir omnivault-myprovider
cd omnivault-myprovider
go mod init github.com/yourorg/omnivault-myprovider

docs.title: 2. Import only the vault package

go get github.com/plexusone/omnivault/vault

docs.title: 3. Implement the interface
docs.text:
package myprovider

import (
    "context"
    "github.com/plexusone/omnivault/vault"
)

type Provider struct {
    client *MyBackendClient
}

type Config struct {
    APIKey   string
    Endpoint string
}

func New(cfg Config) (vault.Vault, error) {
    client, err := newBackendClient(cfg.APIKey, cfg.Endpoint)
    if err != nil {
        return nil, err
    }
    return &Provider{client: client}, nil
}

func (p *Provider) Get(ctx context.Context, path string) (*vault.Secret, error) {
    data, err := p.client.Fetch(ctx, path)
    if err != nil {
        if isNotFound(err) {
            return nil, vault.ErrSecretNotFound
        }
        return nil, err
    }

    return &vault.Secret{
        Value: data.Value,
        Fields: data.Fields,
        Metadata: vault.Metadata{
            CreatedAt: data.CreatedAt,
        },
    }, nil
}

func (p *Provider) Set(ctx context.Context, path string, secret *vault.Secret) error {
    return p.client.Store(ctx, path, secret.Value, secret.Fields)
}

func (p *Provider) Delete(ctx context.Context, path string) error {
    return p.client.Remove(ctx, path)
}

func (p *Provider) Exists(ctx context.Context, path string) (bool, error) {
    _, err := p.client.Fetch(ctx, path)
    if err != nil {
        if isNotFound(err) {
            return false, nil
        }
        return false, err
    }
    return true, nil
}

func (p *Provider) List(ctx context.Context, prefix string) ([]string, error) {
    return p.client.ListKeys(ctx, prefix)
}

func (p *Provider) Name() string {
    return "myprovider"
}

func (p *Provider) Capabilities() vault.Capabilities {
    return vault.Capabilities{
        Read:       true,
        Write:      true,
        Delete:     true,
        List:       true,
        Binary:     false,
        MultiField: true,
    }
}

func (p *Provider) Close() error {
    return p.client.Close()
}

Be accurate about what your provider supports:

        Read:       true,   // Always true for a useful provider
        Write:      false,  // Set false if read-only

docs.title: Module Architecture
docs.text:
omnivault-myprovider/
├── go.mod
├── go.sum

docs.title: Environment Variables
docs.text:
Read secrets from environment variables:

import "github.com/plexusone/omnivault/providers/env"

provider := env.New()

// Or use with client
client, _ := omnivault.NewClient(omnivault.Config{
    Provider: omnivault.ProviderEnv,
})
Capability Supported Read Yes Write No Delete No List No

resolver.Register("env", env.New())
value, _ := resolver.Resolve(ctx, "env://API_KEY")

docs.title: File
docs.text:
Read secrets from files:

import "github.com/plexusone/omnivault/providers/file"

provider := file.New(file.Config{
    Directory: "/etc/secrets",
})

// Or use with client
client, _ := omnivault.NewClient(omnivault.Config{
    Provider: omnivault.ProviderFile,
})
Capability Supported Read Yes Write Yes Delete Yes List Yes

A secret path names a file inside Directory. Paths that are empty, absolute, or climb out of the directory with .. are rejected with vault.ErrInvalidPath, and a symbolic link inside the directory cannot be followed to a file outside it.

Get refuses a secret file that group or others can access (any mode bit in 0077) with file.ErrInsecurePermissions; restrict the file with chmod 600. Where the mode is outside your control, for example a Kubernetes secret volume mounted with the default mode 0644, set defaultMode: 0600 on the volume or, if access is restricted some other way, set AllowInsecurePermissions: true. Windows does not enforce file modes and is never refused.

URI Scheme: file://

resolver.Register("file", file.New(file.Config{Directory: "/etc/secrets"}))
value, _ := resolver.Resolve(ctx, "file://database/password")

package main

import (
    "context"
    "fmt"
    "log"

    "github.com/plexusone/omnivault"

func main() {
    ctx := context.Background()

    // Create client with environment variable provider
    client, err := omnivault.NewClient(omnivault.Config{
        Provider: omnivault.ProviderEnv,
    })
    if err != nil {
        log.Fatal(err)

docs.title: Multi-Provider Resolution
docs.text:
Use the resolver to access secrets from multiple providers using URIs:

package main

import (
    "context"
    "fmt"

    "github.com/plexusone/omnivault"
    "github.com/plexusone/omnivault/providers/env"
    "github.com/plexusone/omnivault/providers/memory"
)

func main() {
    ctx := context.Background()

    // Create resolver with multiple providers
    resolver := omnivault.NewResolver()
    resolver.Register("env", env.New())
    resolver.Register("memory", memory.NewWithSecrets(map[string]string{
        "database/password": "secret123",
    }))

    // Resolve secrets from different providers using URIs
    apiKey, _ := resolver.Resolve(ctx, "env://API_KEY")
    dbPass, _ := resolver.Resolve(ctx, "memory://database/password")

    fmt.Println("API Key:", apiKey)
    fmt.Println("DB Password:", dbPass)
}

package main

    "github.com/plexusone/omnivault-keyring"

func main() {
    ctx := context.Background()

    awsProvider, _ := aws.NewSecretsManager(aws.Config{Region: "us-east-1"})

docs.title: ResolveString
docs.text:
Resolve if it's a URI, otherwise return as-is:

// If input is a URI, resolves it
// If input is a plain string, returns it unchanged
value, err := resolver.ResolveString(ctx, maybeSecretRef)

This is useful when a value might be either a literal or a secret reference:

config := map[string]string{
    "api_key":  "env://API_KEY",      // Will be resolved
    "timeout":  "30s",                 // Returned as-is
}

for key, val := range config {
    resolved, _ := resolver.ResolveString(ctx, val)
    // Use resolved value
}

docs.title: ResolveMap
docs.text:
Resolve all values in a map:

config := map[string]string{
    "database_url": "aws-sm://prod/database#url",
    "api_key":      "env://API_KEY",
    "timeout":      "30s",
}

resolved, err := resolver.ResolveMap(ctx, config)
// resolved["database_url"] = actual database URL
// resolved["api_key"] = actual API key
// resolved["timeout"] = "30s" (unchanged)

resolver := omnivault.NewResolver()
resolver.Register("env", env.New())
resolver.Register("aws-sm", awsProvider)

Add providers at runtime:

// Add a new provider

// Check if a scheme is registered
if resolver.HasScheme("vault") {

docs.text:
value, err := resolver.Resolve(ctx, "unknown://secret")
if err != nil {

}

docs.title: Configuration Loading
docs.text:
type Config struct {
    DatabaseURL string `json:"database_url"`
    APIKey      string `json:"api_key"`
    Debug       bool   `json:"debug"`
}

func LoadConfig(resolver *omnivault.Resolver) (*Config, error) {
    // Load raw config (might contain secret references)
    raw := loadRawConfig()

    // Resolve secrets
    dbURL, err := resolver.ResolveString(ctx, raw.DatabaseURL)
    if err != nil {
        return nil, err
    }

    apiKey, err := resolver.ResolveString(ctx, raw.APIKey)
    if err != nil {
        return nil, err
    }

    return &Config{
        DatabaseURL: dbURL,
        APIKey:      apiKey,
        Debug:       raw.Debug,
    }, nil
}

docs.title: Environment-Based Provider Selection
docs.text:
func setupResolver(env string) *omnivault.Resolver {
    resolver := omnivault.NewResolver()

    switch env {
    case "production":
        awsProvider, _ := aws.NewSecretsManager(aws.Config{
            Region: "us-east-1",
        })
        resolver.Register("secrets", awsProvider)

    case "development":
        resolver.Register("secrets", env.New())
    }

    return resolver
}

docs.title: Release Notes - v0.1.0
docs.text:
Release Date: 2025-01-01

Initial release of OmniVault, a unified Go library for secret management across multiple providers.

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• Unified Interface: Single vault.Vault interface for all secret storage backends
  • Extensible Architecture: Add custom providers as separate Go modules
  • URI-Based Resolution: Reference secrets using URIs like env://API_KEY or aws-sm://secret-name
  • Zero External Dependencies: Core library requires only the Go standard library

docs.title: Core Interface (vault.Vault)
docs.text:
A unified interface for secret management with full CRUD operations:

type Vault interface {
    Get(ctx context.Context, path string) (*Secret, error)
    Set(ctx context.Context, path string, secret *Secret) error
    Delete(ctx context.Context, path string) error
    Exists(ctx context.Context, path string) (bool, error)
    List(ctx context.Context, prefix string) ([]string, error)
    Name() string
    Capabilities() Capabilities
    Close() error
}

docs.title: Built-in Providers
docs.text: Provider Scheme Description Environment Variables env:// Read from os.Getenv() File file:// File-based storage Memory memory:// In-memory storage (for testing)

docs.title: Client API
docs.text:
High-level client with convenience methods:

// Create client
client, err := omnivault.NewClient(omnivault.Config{
    Provider: omnivault.ProviderEnv,
})

// Basic operations
secret, err := client.Get(ctx, "path")
err := client.Set(ctx, "path", &omnivault.Secret{Value: "secret"})
err := client.Delete(ctx, "path")
exists, err := client.Exists(ctx, "path")
paths, err := client.List(ctx, "prefix")

// Convenience methods
value, err := client.GetValue(ctx, "path")
value, err := client.GetField(ctx, "path", "field")
err := client.SetValue(ctx, "path", "value")

// Must variants (panic on error)
secret := client.MustGet(ctx, "path")
value := client.MustGetValue(ctx, "path")

docs.title: URI-Based Resolution
docs.text:
Resolve secrets from multiple providers using URIs:

resolver := omnivault.NewResolver()
resolver.Register("env", envProvider)
resolver.Register("aws-sm", awsProvider)

// Resolve from different providers
apiKey, _ := resolver.Resolve(ctx, "env://API_KEY")
dbPass, _ := resolver.Resolve(ctx, "aws-sm://database/password")

// Resolve if it's a secret reference, otherwise return as-is
value, _ := resolver.ResolveString(ctx, maybeSecretRef)

// Resolve all values in a map
resolved, _ := resolver.ResolveMap(ctx, configMap)

docs.title: Secret Model
docs.text:
Rich secret model with metadata support:

secret := &omnivault.Secret{
    Value: "my-secret-value",
    Fields: map[string]string{
        "username": "admin",
        "password": "secret",
    },
    Metadata: omnivault.Metadata{
        Tags: map[string]string{"env": "prod"},
    },
}

// Access values
value := secret.String()              // Primary value
field := secret.GetField("username")  // Specific field
bytes := secret.Bytes()               // As bytes

Create custom providers as separate Go modules:

package myprovider

import "github.com/plexusone/omnivault/vault"

type Provider struct{}

func New() vault.Vault {
    return &Provider{}
}

// Implement vault.Vault interface...

Use with OmniVault:

client, _ := omnivault.NewClient(omnivault.Config{
    CustomVault: myprovider.New(),
})

docs.title: Release Notes - v0.6.0
docs.text: Release Date: 2026-10-25

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
OmniVault v0.6.0 is a security release. Secrets no longer print their value when formatted or logged, and the file provider keeps secret paths inside its directory and refuses secret files that other users can read. It also adds a SQL table-backed provider for applications that need a self-contained store before moving to an external vault.

This release contains breaking changes. Most importantly, Secret.String is removed: code that reads a secret's value must call Secret.Reveal instead. See Upgrading.

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• Secrets print as [REDACTED] through fmt and log/slog
  • Secret.String removed; Secret.Reveal returns the value
  • File provider refuses paths that leave its directory and secret files readable by group or others
  • New sql:// provider storing encrypted secrets in an application-owned SQL table

docs.title: Secrets redacted when formatted or logged
docs.text:
Secret.String returned the plaintext value, so passing a secret to fmt, wrapping it into an error with %v, or logging it with log/slog wrote the value into logs. Formatting a Secret value (not a pointer) also printed its Value and Fields.

GoString, Format and LogValue now produce [REDACTED] (the constant vault.Redacted) for both Secret and *Secret, for every fmt verb (%v, %+v, %#v, %s, %q, %x, ...) and for log/slog. String is removed rather than redacted, so code that called it to read the value fails to compile instead of silently using the redaction marker as the secret. JSON encoding is unchanged, since providers use it to store and transfer secrets.

docs.title: File provider: paths stay inside the directory
docs.text:
The file provider joined the secret path onto its directory without checking the result, so a path such as ../other/secret read, wrote or deleted files outside the directory, and a symbolic link inside the directory could point anywhere.

Secret paths must now be local: non-empty, not absolute, and with no .. segments that leave the directory. Other paths fail with vault.ErrInvalidPath (also omnivault.ErrInvalidPath). Files are opened through os.Root, which also refuses symbolic links that resolve outside the directory.

docs.title: File provider: secret files must be private
docs.text:
The file provider wrote secret files with a private mode but read any file regardless of its mode, so a secret left group- or world-readable was accepted silently.

Get now checks the mode of the opened file and returns an error matching file.ErrInsecurePermissions when group or others can access it (any bit in 0077). The new Config.AllowInsecurePermissions restores the previous behaviour where the mode cannot be changed. Platforms that do not enforce file modes, such as Windows, are unaffected.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Secret.Reveal: Returns the primary value: ValueBytes as a string if set, otherwise Value
  • vault.Redacted: The marker a secret prints as
  • file.Config.AllowInsecurePermissions and file.ErrInsecurePermissions
  • SQL Store Provider (providers/sqlstore): AES-GCM encrypted secrets in an application-owned table, for MySQL-compatible databases (including Dolt), PostgreSQL and SQLite, with optional auto-migration and a read-only mode
  • ProviderSQL and the SQLConfig alias, so sql:// URIs resolve through the same config-based dispatch as the other built-in providers

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• The module now requires Go 1.26
  • Bump github.com/grokify/oscompat from 0.3.0 to 0.9.0
  • Bump golang.org/x/crypto from 0.52.0 to 0.57.0
  • Bump golang.org/x/term from 0.43.0 to 0.46.0

docs.title: Reading a Secret
docs.text:
secret, err := client.Get(ctx, "database/password")
if err != nil {
    return err
}

dsn := buildDSN(secret.Reveal()) // the value
raw := secret.Bytes()            // the value as bytes

log.Printf("loaded %v", secret)       // loaded [REDACTED]
slog.Info("loaded", "secret", secret) // secret=[REDACTED]

docs.title: SQL Store Provider
docs.text:
import "github.com/plexusone/omnivault/providers/sqlstore"

provider, err := sqlstore.New(sqlstore.Config{
    DB:            db, // an open *sql.DB; the caller owns it
    Table:         "app_vault_secrets",
    Dialect:       sqlstore.DialectPostgres,
    EncryptionKey: key, // 16, 24 or 32 bytes, kept outside this database
    AutoMigrate:   true,
})
if err != nil {
    return err
}
resolver.Register("sql", provider)

dsn, err := resolver.Resolve(ctx, "sql://reporting/warehouse-dsn")

The table stores encrypted payloads only. Keep the encryption key outside the same database, for example in env://, the OS keyring or a cloud secret manager.

docs.title: Upgrading
docs.text: Many downstream modules use OmniVault. Work through every step below in each module that depends on it, including provider modules that construct or read vault.Secret values.

docs.title: 1. Replace Secret.String() with Secret.Reveal()
docs.text:
String no longer exists, so every call is a compile error that points at the line to change:

// Before
value := secret.String()

// After
value := secret.Reveal()

Reveal returns exactly what String used to return. Bytes() is unchanged if you need the value as bytes.

docs.title: 2. Find values read by formatting a secret
docs.text:
Code that read the value by formatting the secret still compiles, but now receives [REDACTED] instead of the value. Search for secrets passed to fmt functions and replace them with Reveal:

// Before: these used to yield the value and now yield "[REDACTED]"
header := fmt.Sprintf("Bearer %s", secret)
value := fmt.Sprint(secret)

// After
header := "Bearer " + secret.Reveal()
value := secret.Reveal()

A search such as the following lists likely places; check each hit where the formatted argument is a vault.Secret or *vault.Secret:

grep -rnE 'fmt\.(Sprint|Sprintf|Sprintln|Fprint|Fprintf|Errorf)\(.*[Ss]ecret' --include='*.go' .

Tests that compared a formatted secret with its value need the same change.

docs.title: 3. File provider: make secret files private
docs.text:
Get refuses a secret file that group or others can access. Restrict each file:

chmod 600 /etc/secrets/database/password

Where the mode is outside your control, for example a Kubernetes secret volume mounted with the default mode 0644, set defaultMode: 0600 on the volume. If access is restricted some other way, opt out explicitly:

provider := file.New(file.Config{
    Directory:                "/etc/secrets",
    AllowInsecurePermissions: true,
})

docs.title: 4. File provider: use paths inside the directory
docs.text: Secret paths are relative to Directory. Paths that are empty, absolute or contain .. segments leaving the directory now fail with vault.ErrInvalidPath, and a symbolic link that resolves outside the directory is refused. Move such secrets into the directory, or point a separate file provider at their location.

docs.title: 5. Update the module
docs.text:
